Settlement coverage demonstrates completion for a pre-cutoff BUILD, holding for a post-cutoff BUILD without code review, and leaving a draft unsettled; it does not demonstrate the plan’s required pre-cutoff-without-override held case, which is reported as a finding.

submitted.functionalSummary: Story c5b49ff953a9a295/s1 (ISSUE-c5b49ff953a9a295): every trivial change gets an ISSUE record. t1 adds meta.kind ('defect'|'change') to the ISSUE, stored by finalizeIssue (unknown refused), rendered as What was asked / Why / Change, with change wording in issue.capture. t2: nextAfterIssue carries the ISSUE hash as standalone.epicHash (small) / params.epicHash (sized), refusing a bad hash. t3: a no-LLD build no longer mints a focus hash; implement and validate refuse without epicHash (no-identity) or without an approved ISSUE (no-head); trivial-build tests seed an ISSUE. t4: triage routes trivial to the issue stage (kind change, magnitude small); no tier starts at build. t5: steering, tool descriptions, the code-review guide and the plan doc follow. t6/t7: a repair step backfill-issue (before units) writes a kind-change ISSUE for each headless standalone trivial BUILD from its focus, rationale and summary, under its hash and anchor, approved by the migration (or pending for an unapproved BUILD); settle then completes or holds the Stories by the existing rule. Known deviation: the plan's t7 test name says a pre-cutoff approval without an override is held; settle.ts completes it, so the test asserts the real rule (a post-cutoff approval with no code review is held). Not done here: the post-deploy repair run on this repository.
